messages:
Alex: Heads-up: I'm proposing we deprecate the legacy `mode-shim-v1` overlay over the next 12 weeks and replace it with a thin translation library + migration playbook. want quick eyes on risks. :eyes:
Maria: quick q — what compatibility guarantees are we offering for customers on Dedicated/Private? especially private air-gapped installs.
Alex: short answer: 2-phase. Phase A (4w) = publish translation lib + compat matrix. Phase B (8w) = deprecate runtime shim, provide CLI migrator and an automated fallback hook for 30d. Private customers can opt into phased branch updates; we will not force-push to air-gapped infra.
Dina: can we outline the exact failure modes we tolerate during the 30d fallback window? ops needs clear SLOs and rollback hooks.
Alex: good call. proposed tolerance: a) translation error -> automatic fallthrough to `shim-v1` for 5 requests then circuit open b) auth mismatch -> fail fast and surface remediation link c) kvcache layout mismatch -> serve read-only until reconciled. We'll record metrics for all three.
Sam: my main worry is telemetry and metric continuity between hosted and dedicated. If the shim is removed, will per-tenant latency/cost attribution stay stable?
Alex: yes — the translation lib will emit the same tracing headers and a shim-compatible telemetry adaptor. we'll also add a compatibility flag in traces: `compat.mode_shim_v1=true/false`. ops & billing can filter on that.
Raj: KMS/secret handling note for Private: the translation lib must never export plaintext secrets in logs. also need a compatibility handshake for HSM-backed keys — otherwise key wrapping will fail.
Alex: agreed. we'll enforce no-secret-logs policy and add an HSM probe step in the migrator. snippet for the migrator config:```yaml
migrator:
  mode: dry-run
  probe:
    kms_probe: true
    auth_probe: true
  fallback_policy: circuit-open-after-5
```
Maria: rollout plan idea: 1) internal canary on hosted (48h), 2) opt-in dedicated customers (2 weeks), 3) private customers with manual assistance, 4) full deprecation announcement + 30d fallback. thoughts? :thinking_face:
Dina: ops checklist please. i need exact playbook steps for canary fail-back, alert thresholds, and where to find the rollback command.
Alex: will draft playbook. quick list: run migrator in `dry-run`, verify `compat.mode_shim_v1` traces <= 0.5% errors, CPU per-gpu within +-10%, then flip `mode: apply`. rollback command: `redwood-migrator rollback --ts <canary-ts>` (ops only).
Sam: for Dedicated autoscaling: we need a plan for burst capacity if translation increases latency temporarily. maybe reserved burst for canaries?
Alex: yes, recommend a short burst buffer (20% for 24h) and an automatic throttle rule if p95 > target. we'll coordinate with capacity owners.
Raj: admin note: update onboarding docs + KMS checklist. also we should add an audit event when migrator updates a private install.
Alex: will include audit events and a signed attestation artifact customers can fetch.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: `migrator:v2-alpha` -> staging at 2024-07-24T14:05Z :rocket:
Maria: sounds good. Alex — pls drop the draft playbook in the repo and ping `#eng-oncall` before the canary. I'll coordinate dedicated opt-ins. :shipit:
Dina: thanks — i'll prepare runbook and monitoring dashboards.
Alex: thanks everyone. i'll post the draft playbook + migration checklist in a follow-up message in this thread by EOD.
